title: KS79356, a novel kynureninase inhibitor, suppresses triple-negative breast cancer progression by attenuating the TNF-alpha/NFkappaB-CD44-Akt signaling axis.
authors: Alghamdi, Maha Alamodi; Deshpande, Hemali; Kumar, Ashish; Rajagopalan, Prasanna
one_liner_zh: 该文研究KYNU小分子抑制剂KS79356对三阴性乳腺癌的抑制作用，虽用分子动力学模拟和MMPBSA分析蛋白-配体结合，但对象为酶-小分子而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅方法部分可借鉴。
abstract: Kynureninase (KYNU), a hydrolase in tryptophan metabolism, has been implicated in cancer progression. However, the therapeutic relevance of targeting KYNU-mediated inflammatory signaling in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains poorly defined High-throughput virtual screening (HTVS) of the ChemBridge library, combined with protein-ligand interaction profiling, molecular dynamics simulations (GROMACS), and binding free energy analysis (GMX_MMPBSA), was employed to identify KYNU inhibitors. In vitro assays were performed in SUM159, MDA-MB-231, and HBL-100 cell lines. KS79356 was identified as the lead compound, displaying strong binding affinity (- 7.8 kcal/mol), stable interactions (RMSD  approximately  0.075 nm), and favorable binding free energy (DeltaG = - 23.93 kcal/mol). KS79356 effectively inhibited KYNU activity (IC(5)(0) = 63.7 nM) and selectively suppressed proliferation of SUM159 (GI(5)(0) = 233 nM) and MDA-MB-231 (GI(5)(0) = 450.8 nM) cells. Mechanistically, KS79356 downregulated TNF-alpha-induced activation of the NFkappaB-CD44-Akt signaling axis, leading to reduced proliferation, invasion, and trans-endothelial migration, while inducing both early and late apoptosis in TNBC cells. By targeting KYNU and attenuating the TNF-alpha/NFkappaB/CD44-Akt signaling axis, KS79356 demonstrates strong antitumor activity in TNBC. These findings highlight the novelty of KYNU as a therapeutic target and support the development of KS79356 as a potential treatment strategy for TNBC progression and metastasis.Clinical trial registrationNot applicable.
abstract_zh: 犬尿氨酸酶（KYNU）是色氨酸代谢中的一种水解酶，已被认为与癌症进展相关。然而，在三阴性乳腺癌（TNBC）中靶向KYNU介导的炎症信号的治疗相关性仍不明确。本研究采用ChemBridge文库的高通量虚拟筛选（HTVS），结合蛋白质-配体相互作用分析、分子动力学模拟（GROMACS）及结合自由能分析（GMX_MMPBSA），以鉴定KYNU抑制剂。在SUM159、MDA-MB-231和HBL-100细胞系中进行了体外实验。KS79356被确定为先导化合物，显示出强结合亲和力（-7.8 kcal/mol）、稳定相互作用（RMSD约0.075 nm）及有利的结合自由能（DeltaG = -23.93 kcal/mol）。KS79356有效抑制KYNU活性（IC(5)(0) = 63.7 nM），并选择性抑制SUM159（GI(5)(0) = 233 nM）和MDA-MB-231（GI(5)(0) = 450.8 nM）细胞的增殖。机制上，KS79356下调TNF-α诱导的NFkappaB-CD44-Akt信号轴的激活，导致增殖、侵袭和跨内皮迁移减少，同时诱导TNBC细胞的早期和晚期凋亡。通过靶向KYNU并减弱TNF-α/NFkappaB/CD44-Akt信号轴，KS79356在TNBC中展现出强效抗肿瘤活性。这些发现凸显了KYNU作为治疗靶点的新颖性，并支持将KS79356开发为针对TNBC进展和转移的潜在治疗策略。临床试验注册：不适用。
